answer: Each identity gets a unique per-epoch prompt, so a Sybil farm cannot paste one answer across a grove of fake accounts; every account must pay for fresh inference. Answers are then scored by a randomly drawn jury that excludes accounts linked by funding source or shared hosts, so the farm cannot grade itself. A comet of cheap new identities gains nothing: each costs real compute every epoch, and a gale of low-effort answers earns zero scores and no reward, so attack cost grows linearly with every fake.
